info.name: ChamPDF API
info.description:
# ChamPDF API

Champions Group's in-house document API. Fill PDF form fields from record data,
apply cryptographic digital signatures with a visible DocuSign-style signature
block, and verify any signed document — plus merge, split, watermark, compress,
OCR, Office conversion, and text/table extraction, all behind one REST API.

Built for server-to-server integration. The Salesforce flow is the reference
implementation and has its own folder below.

---

## Set up in two minutes

1. **Select an environment** — top-right corner. Use **ChamPDF · Production**.
2. **Paste your API key** into the environment's `apiKey` variable (it is typed
   as *secret*, so it is masked and is not exported).
3. **Send `0 · Start here → Who am I`.** A `200` means everything is wired up.

That is all. Auth is set once at the collection level and every request inherits
it — there is no per-request header to maintain.

---

## Base URL

| | |
|---|---|
| **Production** | `https://champdf-api.64.227.154.215.sslip.io` |
| **Interactive docs** | `https://champdf-api.64.227.154.215.sslip.io/docs` |
| **OpenAPI spec** | `https://champdf-api.64.227.154.215.sslip.io/openapi.json` |

`https://champdf.com/api/…` reaches the same backend through the website, but it
adds a proxy hop — prefer the direct host for server-to-server calls. A stable
`api.champdf.com` is being stood up alongside a dedicated container.

> **Build the base URL as configuration, never as a literal.** In this collection
> it is the `baseUrl` variable. In Salesforce it should be a **Named Credential**.
> Then moving to the dedicated host is a config change, never a code edit.

---

## Authentication

Every `/api/v1` call takes a bearer token:

```
Authorization: Bearer champdf_live_...
```

Keys are scoped per endpoint. An out-of-scope call returns `403` with
`{"code":"insufficient_scope","required_scope":"pdf.sign"}` — naming exactly
the scope it needed, so the fix is never a guess.

The `6 · Key management` folder overrides this with the admin token, which is a
separate and more powerful credential.

---

## Limits

| Limit | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| PDF size | 50 MB | Server-side ceiling |
| Burst | 30 requests/min | Per key |
| Monthly quota | Configurable per key | Resets at the start of each **UTC** month |

> **Salesforce callers: the 50 MB ceiling is not reachable from Apex.** Governor
> limits cap a callout body at 6 MB synchronous / 12 MB asynchronous, and heap
> holds the PDF blob, its base64 form and the assembled multipart body at the
> same time. Budget roughly **2 MB sync / 4 MB async** for the PDF itself. Run
> each callout as its own Queueable to get the higher ceiling and to avoid the
> 120-second cumulative callout cap.

---

## Error codes

| Status | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `400` | Bad input — malformed PDF, wrong cert password | Surface `detail` to the user |
| `401` | Missing, malformed or revoked key | Check the environment is selected |
| `403` | `insufficient_scope` — wrong key for this endpoint | Use a key with the named scope |
| `413` | PDF over 50 MB | Compress or split first |
| `422` | Semantic failure — unknown field, unreadable cert, page out of range | `detail` names exactly what is wrong |
| `429` | `rate_limited` (burst) or `quota_exceeded` (monthly) | Back off and retry |
| `503` | Engine not enabled on this deployment | Check `/api/v1/capabilities` first |

Retry on `429` and `5xx`. **Do not blind-retry a timeout** on a signing call —
check whether the artefact landed first. The API is at-least-once and carries no
idempotency key, so de-duplication belongs to the caller.

---

## Data handling

Stateless. Documents and certificates are processed in memory and **never stored
server-side**; the working directory is deleted whatever the outcome. Your system
of record keeps the documents; the signatures live inside the PDFs. API keys are
stored only as SHA-256 hashes and cannot be recovered, even by us.

---

## Working with file uploads in Postman

Most requests here upload a file, and Postman does not export file paths — that
is deliberate, so a shared collection cannot leak your local filesystem. Two
consequences:

- **Sending by hand:** click **Select Files** on the `file` row and choose a
  document. Postman remembers it for that request on your machine.
- **Using the Collection Runner:** set a working directory under
  **Settings → General → Working directory**, put your test files there, and
  Postman will resolve them by name.

*Collection maintained by Champions Group. Verified against production
2026-09-04.*

item.description:
Three zero-risk calls that prove connectivity, auth and feature availability.

Run them top to bottom before anything else. None of them upload a file, so they cost nothing but a request against your quota.

request.description:
Liveness probe. **No authentication.** Returns `200` when the API is up.

If this fails, nothing else will — check `{{baseUrl}}` before debugging your key.

Which optional engines are enabled on this deployment.

Feature-detect with this rather than assuming: any endpoint whose engine is missing returns `503`. For the Salesforce signing flow you need `pdf_sign_advanced` and `pdf_verify` to be `true`.

**The smoke test for your API key.** Returns the key's label, scopes, monthly quota and requests used so far this month.

A `200` here means `{{baseUrl}}` and `{{apiKey}}` are both correct. A `401` means the key is missing, malformed or revoked — check the environment is selected (top-right).

Also the cheapest way to watch quota burn during a load test.

item.name: 1 · Salesforce signing flow
item.description:
**The pipeline that replaces a DocuSign envelope, in the order Apex calls it.**

Steps 1–2 are design-time (run once per template). Steps 3–5 run per document.

### How to run this end to end
Each step consumes the PDF the previous step returned. Postman cannot pipe a binary response body into the next request's file field, so do this manually:

1. Send the request.
2. In the response pane, **Save Response → Save to a file**.
3. Select that file in the next request's `file` field.

It takes about two minutes and it is the fastest way to see the whole pipeline work before writing a line of Apex.

> **Flatten before signing, never after.** Any modification to a signed PDF — including flattening — breaks the signature.

request.description:
Upload your PDF template and get back every AcroForm field: name, type, current value, page and options.

**Design-time only.** Run this once, hard-code the resulting field names in your Apex mapping, and never call it at runtime.

Returns `field_count: 0` for a flat PDF — the API fills existing fields, it cannot add fields to a PDF that has none. Templates must be authored with form fields (any PDF tool, or ChamPDF's web Form Creator).

**Scope:** `pdf.read`

formdata.description: Your PDF template, with AcroForm fields.

request.description:
Fill the template's fields from a JSON object of `{field_name: value}` — in Salesforce, values off the record.

`flatten=true` bakes the values into the page so they render identically everywhere and can no longer be edited. **Always flatten before signing.**

Checkbox fields accept `true`/`false` or `"yes"`/`"no"`.

The response header `X-Fields-Filled` tells you how many fields were written — assert on it. An unknown field name returns `422` naming exactly which names it did not recognise, which makes template drift loud instead of silent.

**Scope:** `pdf.write`

formdata.description: JSON object of field name → value. Must be valid JSON.
Bake values into the page. Always true before signing.

exec: console.log('Save Response → Save to a file, then use it in step 3.');

request.description:
Apply a **PAdES** digital signature and render a visible signature block on the page.

### The visual knobs
The cryptography is identical whatever you set here — these only change what is drawn.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `visible` | `true` draws a signature block. Omit for an invisible signature — still fully valid, still shows in Acrobat's panel. |
| `signature_name` | Rendered in a handwritten script face above the attestation lines. **Visual only** — legal identity always comes from the certificate. |
| `page` | 1-based. `-1` = last page. |
| `x` `y` `width` `height` | Box in PDF points, origin **bottom-left**. A US-Letter page is 612 × 792. |
| `field_name` | Signature field id. Put the Salesforce User Id here — it round-trips through verification. |
| `reason` | Free-text audit line. Put the record Id here. |

### Notes that matter
- `timestamp` defaults to `true` and adds a trusted timestamp from a public TSA, so signing time is not self-asserted. It adds an outbound round-trip — this is the slowest call in the pipeline. Set the Apex callout timeout to 120000 ms.
- **Multiple signers:** run the signed output through this endpoint again with the next certificate, a **unique `field_name`** and a different box position. Each signature is an incremental update, so earlier signatures stay valid.

**Scope:** `pdf.sign`

formdata.description: The signer's `.p12` / `.pfx` certificate. Select the file.
Name in handwritten script. Visual only.
Signature field id — use the Salesforce User Id.
Audit line — use the record Id.
Box left, PDF points from bottom-left.

request.description:
The same cryptographic signature with **no visible block** on the page. Acrobat still shows it in the signature panel and verification is identical.

Use this where a system attestation is wanted but a signature graphic on the document would be wrong.

**Scope:** `pdf.sign`

formdata.description: The signer's `.p12` / `.pfx` certificate. Select the file.
Audit line — use the record Id.

request.description:
Upload any signed PDF and get the integrity report back as JSON. **Store this on the Salesforce record** — it is the audit surface an auditor will ask for.

### Reading the report
- `intact && valid` = signed, and unmodified since. **This is the pass/fail test.** Tampering flips `intact` to `false`.
- `signer` is the certificate's subject — this, not `signature_name`, is the identity that was attested.
- `field` echoes the `field_name` you sent, so the Salesforce User Id round-trips.
- `timestamped: true` means the signing time came from a trusted timestamp authority rather than the signer's clock.

> **`coverage` is not a pass/fail signal.** After a second signer signs, the first signature's coverage is no longer `ENTIRE_FILE` — it covers the revision it signed, which is how every multi-signature PDF works. Test `intact && valid` per signature entry.

**What this does and does not prove:** it reports cryptographic integrity and signer identity. It does **not** assert that the certificate chains to a publicly trusted root — that requires a certificate from a public CA.

**Scope:** `pdf.read`

formdata.description: The signed PDF from step 3 or 4.

response.name: Valid signature
Tampered after signing

exec: pm.test('Every signature is intact and valid', () => r.signatures.forEach(s => { pm.expect(s.intact, 'intact').to.be.true; pm.expect(s.valid, 'valid').to.be.true; }));

item.name: 6 · Key management (admin)
item.description:
Issuing and revoking API keys. **These use the admin token, not an API key** — the collection-level bearer auth is overridden to `noauth` here and the `X-Admin-Token` header is sent instead.

Keep `adminToken` out of any shared environment. It is a different class of credential from an API key: it can mint keys.

request.description:
Create a scoped, quota-limited key.

**The raw key value is returned exactly once, at creation.** The server stores only a SHA-256 hash and cannot recover it. Copy it immediately into your secret store.

### Scopes
| Scope | Grants |
|---|---|
| `pdf.read` | info, to-text, to-images, extract-tables, verify-signature, form-fields |
| `pdf.write` | merge, split, delete-pages, rotate, compress, watermark, from-images, ocr, fill-form |
| `pdf.sign` | sign |
| `pdf` | all of the above |
| `convert` | to-pdf, pdf-to-docx |
| `*` | everything (the default) |

Issue the narrowest scope that works. A `pdf.sign` + `pdf.read` key can sign and verify but cannot alter documents, which limits the blast radius if it leaks.
Every key with its label, scopes, quota and usage. Never returns raw key values.

Revoke by numeric key id (from **List keys**). Takes effect immediately — the next call with that key returns `401`.

Replace the `1` in the URL with the real key id.
